profile.name: Eric Ochieng
profile.title: Ex-Microsoft Product Designer
profile.headline: Making complex experiences feel clear and human.
profile.intro: I’m Eric Ochieng, an ex-Microsoft product designer based in Nairobi. I design experiences that help people find context, understand connections, and get things done.
profile.bio: I’m drawn to complex products, the systems behind human relationships, and AI experiences that are genuinely useful because they respect people’s context and judgment.

projects.title: Accessibility leadership
projects.headline: Leading accessibility from specification through delivery.
projects.summary: Leading accessibility across dozens of projects, from detailed specifications to reflow and high-contrast validation.
projects.problem: Complex people experiences need to remain understandable and operable across assistive technologies, zoom and reflow, contrast modes, keyboard input, and different content states.
projects.team: Design, engineering, product, and accessibility partners
projects.timeframe: Ongoing leadership across dozens of projects
projects.outcome: Accessibility requirements translated into actionable specifications, implementation guidance, and validation.
projects.evidence: Annotated accessibility specifications and validation at 200% reflow and in high-contrast mode.
projects.decisions:
Specify behavior, not only appearance.
Validate reflow at 200%.
Design for high-contrast modes.
Make accessibility part of delivery.
projects.contribution: Led accessibility planning, specification, design review, and validation across dozens of product projects.
projects.result: Helped teams make accessibility an explicit part of product behavior and delivery rather than a final audit.

projects.title: Org sensemaking
projects.headline: Understanding how work really gets done.
projects.summary: Helping people understand project teams, collaboration patterns, and the relationships that shape the work.
projects.problem: Formal reporting structure does not explain who contributes, how collaborators connect, or which working groups shape delivery.
projects.team: Design, product, engineering, and applied AI
projects.outcome: An end-to-end concept connecting conversational intent, a shared workspace, organization context, and collaboration dynamics.
projects.evidence: Product concept screenshots showing the on-ramp, co-creation flow, organization context, and collaboration pods.
projects.decisions:
Start with the job to be done.
Create a durable shared space.
Connect structure with familiarity.
Reveal collaboration patterns.
projects.contribution: Explored the end-to-end organization sensemaking experience and how generated context could remain inspectable and useful.
projects.result: A connected experience model for moving from a broad question to an editable working map.
